elements.evidence: "Company may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience, in whole or in part, at any time"

elements.element: Notice period of 30 days, in writing
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days advance written notice to Contractor"
"Contractor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after such date"

elements.element: No Vendor termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, Contractor may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon ninety (90) days advance written notice" — Contractor's at-will exit is confined to periods with no in-flight SOW
"upon thirty (30) days advance written notice" — shorter than the 60–90 day fallback band

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "without any early termination fee, penalty or accelerated payment" — no fee is imposed, so the cap condition is absent

elements.element: Vendor convenience termination only at end of a term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, Contractor may terminate ... upon ninety (90) days advance written notice"

offending_extra_words: Company shall pay for Services properly performed through the effective date of termination
reasons: The inserted language satisfies every preferred element: a Customer convenience right, 30 days' written notice, refund of prepaid fees for the post-termination period, and a Contractor at-will right confined to periods when no Statement of Work is outstanding (i.e., no Vendor convenience exit during a committed engagement).

Fallback is not independently satisfied because Customer notice is 30 days rather than the 60–90 day band; this is immaterial here since the locked preferred level is met, and the two levels must not be mixed.

Minimality fails: the operation rewrites the whole sub-clause and triples its length (33 to 99 words), adding terms beyond what the preferred position requires — partial/SOW-level termination ('or any Statement of Work', 'in whole or in part'), a payment-for-services-performed mechanic, and duplicative 'penalty or accelerated payment' protection on top of 'without any early termination fee'. A tighter edit granting Company a 30-day convenience right with prepaid-fee refund, plus changing 'fifteen (15)' to 'ninety (90)' and 'either party' to 'Contractor', would suffice.
Intent is preserved: the original 'no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding' condition is retained for Contractor, no defined term is left dangling, and the notice mechanic remains coherent.

Note the deterministic check 'Customer convenience termination present' reports false, which is inconsistent with the rendered operative text quoted above; on a literal reading of the clause the right is expressly granted.
